<BEGIN_SHACL>
@prefix sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
@prefix rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
@prefix qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/> .
@prefix nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#> .
@prefix ex: <https://example.org/shapes/> .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Shape for ships – requirement I2.2.5 applies to each ship instance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:ShipShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:targetClass nltl:ship ;
    sh:message "I2.2.5 – each ship must provide a bottom‑region/lower‑region boundary point." ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path nltl:hasBottomRegionLowerRegionBoundaryPoint ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:node ex:HullBoundaryPointShape ;
        sh:description "The ship must have at least one hull‑boundary point that marks the bottom/lower‑region boundary." ;
    ] .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Shape for the hull‑boundary point that marks the bottom/lower‑region boundary
# (validated via the ship‑shape property, not globally targeted)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:HullBoundaryPointShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:message "I2.2.5 – the boundary point must specify a shell inclination angle of 7°." ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path nltl:shellInclinationAngle ;
        sh:minCount 1 ;
        sh:node ex:ShellInclinationAngleValueShape ;
        sh:description "The boundary point must carry a shell inclination angle quantity." ;
    ] .

# -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Shape for the QuantityValue representing the shell inclination angle
# (validated via the hull‑boundary‑point shape, not globally targeted)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------
ex:ShellInclinationAngleValueShape
    a sh:NodeShape ;
    sh:message "I2.2.5 – the shell inclination angle must be exactly 7 degrees." ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path qudt:numericValue ;
        sh:hasValue "7"^^xsd:decimal ;
        sh:datatype xsd:decimal ;
        sh:description "Numeric value of the angle must be 7." ;
    ] ;
    sh:property [
        sh:path qudt:unit ;
        sh:hasValue <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG> ;
        sh:description "Unit must be degree (deg)." ;
    ] .
<END_SHACL>

We need to repair the previous candidate SHACL to address findings, preserving obligations etc. Findings:

1. ADMISSION_SCOPE_ERROR: "Other target classes select beyond declared population". Means targetClass may be too broad? Admission expects using declared owner_class = https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#ship as population boundary. The shape ex:ShipShape uses sh:targetClass nltl:ship which matches. But maybe other target classes (like ex:HullBoundaryPointShape targeting nltl:hullBoundaryPoint) also select beyond declared population. According to contract (E30), owners mapping shows target_owner null, but modelPaths define fromOwner ship to hullBoundaryPoint via property. So hullBoundaryPoint is not directly in admitted population; must be constrained via path from ship. So we need to remove sh:targetClass on HullBoundaryPointShape and maybe on QuantityValue shape, and instead use sh:nodeConstraint on property path? We can keep shapes but use sh:targetObjectsOf? Actually to enforce activation within admitted population, we should not have independent target classes for non-ship nodes. Instead we can keep shapes as node shapes but not target them globally; they will be applied via sh:node on property. Remove sh:targetClass from HullBoundaryPointShape and ShellInclinationAngleValueShape. Also maybe remove sh:targetClass from QuantityValue shape (qudt:QuantityValue) because that also selects beyond population. Keep ShipShape targetClass.

Thus fix ADMISSION_SCOPE_ERROR.

2. UNRESOLVED_CONTEXT: "Target cannot be bound to an explicit model owner". This is same issue; need to resolve by removing target on non-owner classes.

3. NUMERIC_TERM_REVIEW: value literal "7"^^xsd:decimal; need decide if source requires numeric equality or exact term. The source text says "inclined 7°". Should be exactly 7 degrees; numeric equality fine. But need to use sh:hasValue with datatype decimal and maybe use sh:equals? In SHACL, sh:hasValue checks RDF term equality, but decimals with same lexical form "7" vs "7.0" differ? Source requirement may not require lexical exactness. We should use sh:equals (??). Actually sh:hasValue is term equality, but we can instead use sh:datatype and sh:minInclusive, sh:maxExclusive? To require numeric equality, use sh:equals? No, there is sh:equals for node comparisons. Better use sh:hasValue but also allow lexical variations? Hard. The developer says we may need to retain exact-term matching unless source requires numeric equality. The source didn't specify lexical, only numeric 7°, thus numeric equality acceptable. However SHACL can't do numeric equality except via sh:hasValue with term equality; but we can enforce value via sh:in with "7"^^xsd:decimal; it's same. Likely keep as is.

But we must ensure unit specification. The unit is defined with sh:hasValue <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/DEG>. That's fine.

Potential other issues: need to use proper prefixes for nltl namespace; earlier used nltl: but prefix defines nltl: https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#. Good.

Need to adjust ex:HullBoundaryPointShape and ex:ShellInclinationAngleValueShape to not have sh:targetClass, maybe use sh:targetObjectsOf? Could use sh:targetObjectsOf nltl:hasBottomRegionLowerRegionBoundaryPoint for hullBoundaryPoint? However to validate each hullBoundaryPoint reached from a ship, we already have ex:ShipShape property with sh:node ex:HullBoundaryPointShape, which will validate the object node irrespective of its class. So we can drop targetClass.

Similarly, for QuantityValue shape, we validate via sh:node ex:ShellInclinationAngleValueShape, so no need targetClass.

Thus modify shapes accordingly.

Also maybe need to adjust ex:ShellInclinationAngleValueShape to enforce exact numeric value using sh:equals? Keep as hasValue.

Potential also need to add sh:closed? Not required.

Let's produce repaired SHACL:

Include comments.

Make sure prefixes same.

Remove sh:targetClass from HullBoundaryPointShape and ShellInclinationAngleValueShape.

Make sure shape still has sh:message etc.

Add sh:property constraints same.

Everything else unchanged.

Return <BEGIN_SHACL> ... <END_SHACL>.
